title: "It's really hazardous": Muhlenberg County roads refreeze after winter storm - NewsBreak
text:
By Isaiah Calalang ,
1 hours ago
MUHLENBERG COUNTY, Ky. (WEHT) — Many roads across the Tri-State have begun to clear up but several roads in Muhlenberg County have once again become treacherous after the bitter cold temperatures have caused it to refreeze over night.
“Yesterday it didn’t event seem that bad and then this morning it all refroze,” Greenville waitress Olivia Pointer said. “I was slipping and everything this morning. It was crazy.”
While the winter storm may be over, highway crews in Muhlenberg County say the real work is just beginning. Crews from neighboring counties have been requested to assist after ice as thick as three inches accumulated near the county line.
“The salt is working some,” County Road Superintendent Kelly Richey said. “But when it gets down to the lower 20’s, the salt doesn’t do any good. Mother Nature has not been our friend.”
Pointer is a waitress in Greenville who says staying at home has left her restless. Frustrated with the frozen roadways, she says she’s ready for things to return to normal.
“I was extremely bored,” Pointer said. “I was in my house all day and I didn’t really have anything to do. I was ready to go back to work. I was ready to get out of the house and do something.”
To combat the build up of ice and snow, highway crews are applying additional road salt and salt brine with a little bit of help on the way from some neighbors in Hopkins, Daviess, Hancock, Union and Caldwell counties.
“You’re going to see a lot more KYTC equipment on the road,” KYTC’s Matt Hughes said. “There were plows from Hopkins County when I got here. It really is a team effort. We’re all part of the same district. And in situations like this, all the counties pull together to help each other out.”
The county highway department says even with the additional support on the way, they are urging residents to drive with extreme caution as it will take several more days to clear the roads.
